intro: 60 AI items this week (25 India-relevant) across 8 sources.

items.title: Frontier AI labs still won’t say how they’d contain a rogue model
items.summary: A new study finds leading AI labs have few publicly documented plans for containing rogue models, raising questions about preparedness as AI systems increasingly demonstrate unexpected and potentially dangerous behavior.

items.title: Anthropic’s Opus 4.6 is a smut-machine
items.summary: Anthropic forbids its Claude models from generating sexually explicit content. But a series of tests conducted by TechCrunch found that it didn't take much to get past the restriction.

items.title: Nvidia just showed that the harness, not the AI model, is now the real hero
items.summary: Nvidia research shows that AI agents can perform well, and not go off the deep end, through fine-tuning, even if the AI model isn't that great at the task.

items.title: Ramp launches its own AI model router, called Router
items.summary: Ramp has launched its own AI model routing service, dubbed Router, that lets users and companies use and switch between various large language models via an API.

items.title: Grok exfiltrates user data when malicious instructions are encrypted
items.summary: Cryptographic Context Injection is only the latest way to break an LLM safety guardrail.

items.title: We still don’t know how people are really using AI
items.summary: AI companies like Anthropic and OpenAI regularly publish reports on how people are using products like Claude and ChatGPT, but they only release the data they want us to see, AI researchers say. “There is no independent source to corroborate it,” says Anka Reuel, a computer sc…

items.title: Measuring benchmark optimization in speech recognition
Inherent, founded by DeepMind alumni, says its AI ‘teammate’ just outperformed Anthropic and OpenAI at replicating research
items.summary: Built by DeepMind alumni, British AI lab Inherent released Faraday, an AI agent whose ability to replicate scientific papers could be a stepping stone for innovation.

items.title: Nvidia partners with data center developer Cloverleaf
items.summary: Nvidia continues to pour money into data center development — just as AI data centers bring lots of money into Nvidia.

items.title: Linkdaze’s smart calendar is built to run a household, not just track a schedule
items.summary: Linkdaze's smart digital calendar stands out for not putting its features behind a paywall, including an AI meal planner tool.

items.title: How Much Memory Does Your Agent Actually Need?
Harvard’s $699 startup bootcamp offers AI avatars of its instructors
items.summary: In the HBS Foundry program, AI avatars provide feedback during practice pitches and board meetings.

items.title: OpenAI says California should strengthen its AI safety bill
items.summary: OpenAI is calling for California to strengthen SB 53, an AI safety bill that the company previously opposed.

items.title: Starcloud raises $250 million for orbital data centers as launch options dry up
items.summary: There's about to be a big fight to secure access to space.

items.title: The DOJ is investigating a16z. What does this mean for venture capital?
items.summary: Andreessen Horowitz has two partners sitting on the boards of companies that now compete with each other: Ben Horowitz at Databricks and Martin Casado at Fivetran. Nothing too scandalous on the surface, except the Department of Justice has reportedly been investigating the arr…

items.title: AI data startup Micro1 reaches $500M gross run rate amid AI training boom
items.summary: Surging demand for AI training data is driving rapid growth for the startup and its rivals.

items.title: OpenAI is gaining on Anthropic with business users, new data indicates
items.summary: Businesses are willing to flop back and forth as each lab releases new models, volatility that should give both companies' investors pause about how "sticky" enterprise AI spending really is.

items.title: Software, services, AI: test your business creativity with Edition 246 of our weekly quiz!
items.summary: This insightful feature from YourStory tests and strengthens your business acumen! Here are 5 questions to kick off this 246th quiz. Ready?

items.title: AI volumes may outweigh revenue deflation for IT sector by FY30: Report
items.summary: CLSA said the industry is facing "multiple macro/micro headwinds", but expects AI to eventually create new growth opportunities. It said AI could initially compress revenues as productivity gains are passed on to clients, but "AI volumes could supersede deflation by FY30."

items.title: VCs becoming marginal in AI cycle, enterprises should invest in the sector: Peak XV’s Shailendra Singh
items.summary: “Every large enterprise should be investing in AI,” Singh said at The Economic Times World Leaders Forum in New Delhi. Pointing to HCLTech’s investment in Indian foundational model startup Sarvam AI, and global bets such as Amazon’s backing of Anthropic, he said corporate bala…

items.title: Nvidia invests in data center developer Cloverleaf Infrastructure
items.summary: The investment ⁠will ⁠help Cloverleaf develop sites for the ​data centers, while Nvidia will support infrastructure buildouts for ​AI computing.

items.title: Only 9% of India's finance aspirants feel ready to compete in AI-driven job market: Study
items.summary: The study found that the gap in AI readiness was the widest difference between the two groups. About 56% of Indian respondents said AI and automation were making it slightly or much harder to get their desired job. This was close to the 59% of global graduates who saw AI as a …

items.title: AI capex slowdown could derail India's cyclical recovery, weigh on growth: Nuvama
items.summary: Any slowdown in the global artificial intelligence (AI) capital expenditure boom could pose a significant risk to India's ongoing cyclical recovery, with weaker global demand and commodity prices likely to weigh on corporate revenue and credit growth, while a still narrow dome…

items.title: OpenAI cuts developer pricing for frontier GPT-5.6 Sol model by more than 20%
items.summary: The price cuts ​are effective on OpenAI's application programming interface, or API, and ​are rolling out across eligible plans for credits on its agentic AI product ChatGPT Work ​and its coding tool Codex, ⁠OpenAI said.

items.title: Karnataka govt launches low cost AI computing device KEO
items.summary: The government aims to democratise the access to artificial intelligence (AI) through the introduction of KEO.

careers.note: Demand snapshot for 2026. ML Engineer is the most in-demand AI title; agentic-AI and deep-learning skills carry the highest pay premiums; Python + one cloud is the baseline. Specialisation beats generalisation for freshers.

paths.note: #1 AI title — build, deploy & maintain models in production. Best all-round entry into AI.
RAG, tool-use & multi-agent systems. ~40% of enterprise apps will embed AI agents by year-end.
Neural nets for vision & speech. Highest premiums; usually needs strong maths / grad study.
Ship & scale models on the cloud. Cloud AI certs add 20–25% to salary.
Foundational, widest entry door; a reliable first step into AI.
Imaging, robotics, autonomous systems, medical AI.
Powers chatbots, search & agents — the hottest application area.
5–8 yrs experience; $140k–$332k bands. Translates AI into business value.
Alignment, evals, red-teaming & policy — newer but expanding fast.

fresher.why: The lingua franca of ML — non-negotiable.
Linear algebra, probability & calculus — enough to reason about models.
Regression, classification, evaluation, the ML workflow.
Build & train neural nets; PyTorch dominates research & jobs.
Ship a small LLM app — the most visible skill to recruiters now.
Real AI work is mostly data; SQL is everywhere.
AWS leads (~40% of postings), then Azure & GCP. Version everything.
A deployed project that solves a real problem is the #1 differentiator.

experienced.why: Docker, CI/CD, monitoring, model/versioning — production is where value lives.
Multi-agent orchestration, tool-use, evals — the surging frontier.
AWS/Azure/GCP architecture; certs add a 20–25% salary premium.
Adapt, measure and harden models for a domain.
Cost & latency engineering for large models.
Trade-offs across data, latency, cost & reliability at scale.
CV, NLP, recsys, healthcare — depth beats breadth at senior levels.
Leading teams and tying models to measurable outcomes.
